question: A department head asks for a one-page summary of what Claude will and will not do in a redesigned review workflow. What is the most important thing for that summary to include?
options: A) A technical comparison of the model options so the department can judge the quality of the choice.
B) A ranked list of every Claude feature the department could adopt over the next financial year.
C) A statement that the outputs are reliable enough for review to be dropped once staff are trained.
D) Where Claude drafts and where a named person reviews, with the checks that stay in human hands.
correct_answers: D) Where Claude drafts and where a named person reviews, with the checks that stay in human hands.
explanations: A model comparison is not what a department head needs to understand value and limits.
A feature roadmap does not tell the department what the workflow will and will not do.
Promising that review disappears oversells the tool and removes the accountability step.
Correct. Stakeholders need the boundary between assisted work and human accountability stated plainly.
